Summary Background HFrEF is a heterogenous condition with high mortality. We used serial assessments of 4210 circulating proteins to identify distinct novel protein-based HFrEF subphenotypes and to investigate underlying dynamic biological mechanisms. Herewith we aimed to gain pathophysiological insights and fuel opportunities for personalised treatment. Methods In 382 patients, we performed trimonthly blood sampling during a median follow-up of 2.1 [IQR:1.1–2.6] years. We selected all baseline samples and two samples closest to the primary endpoint (PEP; composite of cardiovascular mortality, HF hospitalization, LVAD implantation, and heart transplantation) or censoring, and applied an aptamer-based multiplex proteomic approach. Using unsupervised machine learning methods, we derived clusters from 4210 repeatedly measured proteomic biomarkers. Sets of proteins that drove cluster allocation were analysed via an enrichment analysis. Differences in clinical characteristics and PEP occurrence were evaluated. Findings We identified four subphenotypes with different protein profiles, prognosis and clinical characteristics, including age (median [IQR] for subphenotypes 1–4, respectively:70 [64, 76], 68 [60, 79], 57 [47, 65], 59 [56, 66]years), EF (30 [26, 36], 26 [20, 38], 26 [22, 32], 33 [28, 37]%), and chronic renal failure (45%, 65%, 36%, 37%). Subphenotype allocation was driven by subsets of proteins associated with various biological functions, such as oxidative stress, inflammation and extracellular matrix organisation. Clinical characteristics of the subphenotypes were aligned with these associations. Subphenotypes 2 and 3 had the worst prognosis compared to subphenotype 1 (adjHR (95%CI):3.43 (1.76–6.69), and 2.88 (1.37–6.03), respectively). Interpretation Four circulating-protein based subphenotypes are present in HFrEF, which are driven by varying combinations of protein subsets, and have different clinical characteristics and prognosis. Keywords Proteomics Biomarkers Phenotypes Unsupervised machine learning Heart Failure Research in context Evidence before this study HFrEF (Heart Failure with reduced Ejection Fraction), as a heterogeneous condition with a high mortality rate, can benefit greatly from subphenotyping efforts. Proteomic blood biomarkers carry large potential for phenotyping studies in the cardiovascular domain, as shown in studies in HFpEF (Heart Failure with preserved Ejection Fraction) patients. Added value of this study In this study, we identify four distinct HFrEF phenotypes based on 4210 repeatedly measured proteomic biomarkers. These subphenotypes show differing protein profiles, clinical characteristics and prognosis. The subphenotypes are driven by subsets of proteins that are associated with various pathophysiological pathways. Novel aspects of this study include the repeated assessments of the proteomic panel, in order to capture dynamic biological mechanisms; and the extensive set of proteins used. Our study demonstrates that repeated proteomics measurements improve the accuracy of subphenotypes in relation to prognosis compared to single baseline measurements. Moreover, the large protein panel provides a comprehensive assessment of the processes involved in heart failure, and gives us the opportunity to associate specific biological pathways and processes with the subphenotypes. Implications of all the available evidence Repeated assessment of extensive biomarker panels can contribute pathophysiological insights for complex diagnoses like HFrEF. Future studies should further investigate the role of these biological mechanisms in HFrEF and further explore prospects of personalized treatment decisions based on subphenotypes.

extracted_data.document_summary: This study investigated novel protein-based subphenotypes in Heart Failure with reduced Ejection Fraction (HFrEF) patients using unsupervised machine learning on 4210 repeatedly measured circulating proteins over a median 2.1-year follow-up in 382 patients. It identified four distinct subphenotypes with varying protein profiles, clinical characteristics (e.g., age, EF, chronic renal failure), and prognosis. These subphenotypes were driven by specific protein subsets associated with various biological mechanisms, including oxidative stress, inflammation, extracellular matrix organization, myocardial stretch/stress, injury, and renal dysfunction. Subphenotypes 2 and 3 demonstrated significantly worse clinical outcomes compared to subphenotype 1, highlighting the value of dynamic proteomic profiling for gaining pathophysiological insights and exploring personalized treatment opportunities in complex diagnoses like HFrEF.

treatment_details.therapy_type: Proteomic profiling and subphenotyping in Heart Failure with reduced Ejection Fraction (HFrEF) patients.
treatment_details.dose_specificity: This was an observational study involving trimonthly blood sampling over a median follow-up of 2.1 years (IQR: 1.1–2.6 years) in 382 HFrEF patients, totaling 1066 blood samples. An aptamer-based multiplex proteomic approach (SOMAscan assay) was used to measure 4210 circulating proteins, yielding relative fluorescence units (RFUs) for comparative analysis rather than absolute concentrations. No specific intervention, treatment, or dose-response comparisons were conducted, as the study focused on characterizing disease subphenotypes and biomarker patterns over time. Repeated proteomic measurements (incorporating both intercept and slope coefficients) demonstrated improved accuracy for survival models (c-index 0.73, BIC 1023) compared to single time-point assessments.

measured_effect.magnitude_quantification: Overall median (IQR) at baseline was 133 (46–274) pmol/L. Subphenotype 2 showed the highest median levels at baseline and elevated levels as part of Subset D, often exceeding three times the normal upper limit. Lowest median levels were observed in subphenotype 3 at baseline.

analyzed_biomarkers.core_biological_function: Indicates cardiac wall stress, myocardial stretch, and ventricular dysfunction, released in response to increased ventricular pressure and volume; a key diagnostic and prognostic biomarker for heart failure severity and fibrosis.
analyzed_biomarkers.relevant_activity_context: Baseline and longitudinal assessment in HFrEF patients for subphenotype identification, particularly defining Subphenotype 2 which is characterized by older patients, lower SBP, increased comorbidities (e.g., diabetes mellitus, chronic renal failure), and very high levels, often contributing to hospitalization criteria for acute or worsened HF.
analyzed_biomarkers.performance_or_health_indicator: Higher levels are strongly associated with worse clinical outcomes, including increased risk of hospitalization due to worsening heart failure, higher heart failure severity, and poorer prognosis (HR 3.43 (1.76–6.69) for Subphenotype 2 vs. Subphenotype 1).

measured_effect.magnitude_quantification: Overall median (IQR) at baseline was 18 (9–33) ng/L. Subphenotype 2 showed the highest median levels at baseline and elevated levels as part of Subset D. Lowest median hs-troponin T was observed in subphenotype 3 at baseline.

analyzed_biomarkers.core_biological_function: Indicates myocardial injury or necrosis, serving as a marker of cardiac damage.
analyzed_biomarkers.relevant_activity_context: Baseline and longitudinal assessment in HFrEF patients for subphenotype identification, particularly defining Subphenotypes 2 (higher levels, worse outcomes) and 3 (lower median, but still worse outcomes).
analyzed_biomarkers.performance_or_health_indicator: Higher levels are strongly associated with subphenotype 2, indicating significant myocardial injury and poorer prognosis. Although levels are lower in subphenotype 3, it is also linked to worse outcomes.

measured_effect.magnitude_quantification: Overall median (IQR) at baseline was 2.2 (0.9–4.9) mg/L. Subphenotype 2 showed the highest median levels, while subphenotype 4 had the lowest median levels. Subphenotype 1 also had lower median levels at baseline. Significantly associated with subphenotype allocation (p < 0.05).

analyzed_biomarkers.core_biological_function: An acute-phase reactant and a robust indicator of systemic inflammation.
analyzed_biomarkers.relevant_activity_context: Baseline assessment in HFrEF patients for subphenotype identification, particularly distinguishing Subphenotypes 1, 2, and 4.
analyzed_biomarkers.performance_or_health_indicator: Highest levels are associated with subphenotype 2, indicating higher inflammatory burden and worse clinical outcomes. Lower levels are associated with subphenotypes 1 (better outcomes) and 4 (no significant outcome association), suggesting a role in stratifying prognosis based on inflammatory status.
